 #### [6. Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ref_=ls_t_6) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

Clinton Eastwood Jr. was born May 31, 1930 in San Francisco, to Clinton Eastwood Sr., a bond salesman and later manufacturing executive for Georgia-Pacific Corporation, and [Ruth Wood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2503495/?ls) (née Margret Ruth Runner), a housewife turned IBM clerk. He grew up in nearby Piedmont. At school Clint took interest in music and mechanics, but was an otherwise bored student; this resulted in being held back a grade.  
  
In 1949, the year he graduated from high school, his parents and younger sister Jeanne moved to Seattle. Clint spent a couple years in the Pacific Northwest himself, operating log broncs in Springfield, Oregon, with summer gigs life-guarding in Renton, Washington. Returning to California in 1951, he did a two-year stint at Fort Ord Military Reservation and later enrolled at L.A. City College, but dropped out to pursue acting.  
  
During the mid-1950s he landed uncredited bit parts in such Z movies as [Revenge of the Creature (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048554/?ls) and [Tarantula (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048696/?ls) while digging swimming pools and driving a garbage truck to supplement his income. In 1958, he landed his first consequential acting role in the long-running TV show [Rawhide (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052504/?ls) with [Eric Fleming](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281661/?ls). Although only a secondary player the first seven seasons, he was promoted to series star when Fleming departed--both literally and figuratively--in its final year, along the way becoming a recognizable face to television viewers around the country.  
  
Eastwood's big-screen breakthrough came as The Man with No Name in [Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ls)'s trilogy of excellent spaghetti westerns: [A Fistful of Dollars (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058461/?ls), [For a Few Dollars More (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059578/?ls), and [The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060196/?ls). The movies were shown exclusively in Italy during their respective copyright years with [Enrico Maria Salerno](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0758066/?ls) providing the voice of Eastwood's character, finally getting American distribution in 1967-68. As the last film racked up respectable grosses, Eastwood, 37, rose from a barely registering actor to sought-after commodity in just a matter of months. Again a success was the late-blooming star's first U.S.-made western, [Hang 'Em High (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061747/?ls). He followed that up with the lead role in [Coogan's Bluff (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062824/?ls) (the loose inspiration for the TV series [McCloud (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065317/?ls)), before playing second fiddle to [Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ls) in the World War II epic [Where Eagles Dare (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065207/?ls) and [Lee Marvin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001511/?ls) in the bizarre musical [Paint Your Wagon (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064782/?ls). In [Two Mules for Sister Sara (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065134/?ls) and [Kelly's Heroes (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065938/?ls), Eastwood leaned in an experimental direction by combining tough-guy action with offbeat humor.  
  
1971 proved to be his busiest year in film. He starred as a sleazy Union soldier in [The Beguiled (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066819/?ls) to critical acclaim, and made his directorial debut with the classic erotic thriller [Play Misty for Me (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067588/?ls). His role as the hard edge police inspector in [Dirty Harry (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066999/?ls), meanwhile, boosted him to cultural icon status and helped popularize the loose-cannon cop genre. Eastwood put out a steady stream of entertaining movies thereafter: the westerns [Joe Kidd (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068768/?ls), [High Plains Drifter (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068699/?ls) and [The Outlaw Josey Wales (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075029/?ls) (his first of six onscreen collaborations with then live-in love [Sondra Locke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0516800/?ls)), the Dirty Harry sequels [Magnum Force (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070355/?ls) and [The Enforcer (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074483/?ls), the action-packed road adventures [Thunderbolt and Lightfoot (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072288/?ls) and [The Gauntlet (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076070/?ls), and the prison film [Escape from Alcatraz (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079116/?ls). He branched out into the comedy genre in 1978 with [Every Which Way But Loose (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077523/?ls), which became the biggest hit of his career up to that time; taking inflation into account, it still is. In short, [The Eiger Sanction (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072926/?ls) notwithstanding, the 1970s were nonstop success for Eastwood.  
  
Eastwood kicked off the 1980s with [Any Which Way You Can (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080377/?ls), the blockbuster sequel to Every Which Way but Loose. The fourth Dirty Harry film, [Sudden Impact (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086383/?ls), was the highest-grossing film of the franchise and spawned his trademark catchphrase: "Make my day." He also starred in [Bronco Billy (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080472/?ls), [Firefox (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083943/?ls), [Tightrope (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088272/?ls), [City Heat (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087062/?ls), [Pale Rider (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089767/?ls) and [Heartbreak Ridge (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091187/?ls), all of which were solid hits, with [Honkytonk Man (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084088/?ls) being his only commercial failure of the period. In 1988, he did his fifth and final Dirty Harry movie, [The Dead Pool (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094963/?ls). Although it was a success overall, it did not have the box office punch the previous films had. About this time, with outright bombs like [Pink Cadillac (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098097/?ls) and [The Rookie (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100514/?ls), it seemed Eastwood's star was declining as it never had before. He then started taking on low-key projects, directing [Bird (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094747/?ls), a biopic of [Charlie Parker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0662127/?ls) that earned him a Golden Globe, and starring in and directing [White Hunter Black Heart (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100928/?ls), an uneven, loose biopic of [John Huston](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001379/?ls) (both films had a limited release).  
  
Eastwood bounced back big time with his dark western [Unforgiven (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105695/?ls), which garnered the then 62-year-old his first ever Academy Award nomination (Best Actor), and an Oscar win for Best Director. Churning out a quick follow-up hit, he took on the secret service in [In the Line of Fire (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107206/?ls), then accepted second billing for the first time since 1970 in the interesting but poorly received [A Perfect World (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107808/?ls) with [Kevin Costner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000126/?ls). Next was a love story, [The Bridges of Madison County (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112579/?ls), where Eastwood surprised audiences with a sensitive performance alongside none other than [Meryl Streep](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000658/?ls). But it soon became apparent he was going backwards after his brief revival. Subsequent films were credible, but nothing really stuck out. [Absolute Power (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118548/?ls) and [Space Cowboys (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0186566/?ls) did well enough, while [True Crime (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0139668/?ls) and [Blood Work (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0309377/?ls) were received badly, as was [Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119668/?ls), which he directed but didn't appear in.  
  
Eastwood surprised again in the mid-2000s, returning to the top of the A-list with [Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ls). Also starring [Hilary Swank](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005476/?ls) and [Morgan Freeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000151/?ls), the hugely successful drama won four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director for Eastwood. He scored his second Best Actor nomination, too. His next starring vehicle, [Gran Torino (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1205489/?ls), earned almost $30 million in its opening weekend and was his highest grosser unadjusted for inflation. 2012 saw him in a rare lighthearted movie, [Trouble with the Curve (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2083383/?ls), as well as a reality show, [Mrs. Eastwood & Company (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2305717/?ls).  
  
Between acting jobs, he chalked up an impressive list of credits behind the camera. He directed [Mystic River (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0327056/?ls) (in which [Sean Penn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000576/?ls) and [Tim Robbins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000209/?ls) gave Oscar-winning performances), [Flags of Our Fathers (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0418689/?ls), [Letters from Iwo Jima (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0498380/?ls) (nominated for the Best Picture Oscar), [Changeling (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0824747/?ls) (a vehicle for [Angelina Jolie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001401/?ls)), [Invictus (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1057500/?ls) (again with Freeman), [Hereafter (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1212419/?ls), [J. Edgar (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1616195/?ls), [Jersey Boys (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1742044/?ls), [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ls) (2014's top box office champ), [Sully (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3263904/?ls) (starring [Tom Hanks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000158/?ls) as hero pilot [Chesley Sullenberger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3314810/?ls)) and [The 15:17 to Paris (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6802308/?ls). Back on screens after a considerable absence, he played an unlikely drug courier in [The Mule (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7959026/?ls), which reached the top of the box office with a nine-figure gross, then directed [Richard Jewell (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3513548/?ls). At age 91, Eastwood made history as the oldest actor to star above the title in a movie with the release of [Cry Macho (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1924245/?ls).  
  
Away from the limelight, Eastwood has led an aberrant existence and is described by biographer [Patrick McGilligan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0569292/?ls) as a cunning manipulator of the media. His convoluted slew of partners and children are now somewhat factually acknowledged, but for the first three decades of his celebrity, his personal life was kept top secret, and several of his families were left out of the official narrative. The actor refuses to disclose his exact number of offspring even to this day. He had a longtime relationship with similarly abstruse co-star Locke (who died aged 74 in 2018, though for her entire public life she masqueraded about being younger), and has fathered at least eight children by at least six different women in an unending string of liaisons, many of which overlapped. He has been married only twice, however, with a mere three of his progeny coming from those unions.  
  
His known children are: [Laurie Murray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm15158933/?ls) (b. 1954), whose mother is unidentified; [Kimber Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247761/?ls) (b. 1964) with stuntwoman [Roxanne Tunis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0876651/?ls); [Kyle Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247762/?ls) (b. 1968) and [Alison Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002055/?ls) (b. 1972) with his first ex-wife, [Margaret Neville Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1527881/?ls); [Scott Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2207222/?ls) (b. 1986) and [Kathryn Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1828228/?ls) (b. 1988) with stewardess Jacelyn Reeves; [Francesca Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247754/?ls) (b. 1993) with actress [Frances Fisher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004920/?ls); and [Morgan Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1765859/?ls) (b. 1996) with his second ex-wife, [Dina Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247753/?ls). The entire time that he lived with Locke she was legally married to sculptor [Gordon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026770/?ls).  
  
Eastwood has real estate holdings in Bel-Air, La Quinta, Carmel-by-the-Sea, Cassel (in remote northern California), Idaho's Sun Valley and Kihei, Hawaii.

 #### [8. Elvis Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000062/?ref_=ls_t_8) 

    *   Music Artist
    *   Actor
    *   Music Department

[Tickle Me (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056585/?ref_=ls_knf_8)

Elvis Aaron Presley was born on January 8, 1935 in East Tupelo, Mississippi, to [Gladys Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0696175/?ls) (née Gladys Love Smith) and [Vernon Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0696184/?ls) (Vernon Elvis Presley). He had a twin brother who was stillborn. In 1948, Elvis and his parents moved to Memphis, Tennessee where he attended Humes High School. In 1953, he attended the senior prom with the current girl he was courting, Regis Wilson. After graduating from high school in Memphis, Elvis took odd jobs working as a movie theater usher and a truck driver for Crown Electric Company. He began singing locally as "The Hillbilly Cat", then signed with a local recording company, and then with RCA in 1955.  
  
Elvis did much to establish early rock and roll music. He began his career as a performer of rockabilly, an up-tempo fusion of country music and rhythm and blues, with a strong backbeat. His novel versions of existing songs, mixing 'black' and 'white' sounds, made him popular - and controversial - as did his uninhibited stage and television performances. He recorded songs in the rock and roll genre, with tracks like "Jailhouse Rock" and "Hound Dog" later embodying the style. Presley had a versatile voice and had unusually wide success encompassing other genres, including gospel, blues, ballads and pop music. Teenage girls became hysterical over his blatantly sexual gyrations, particularly the one that got him nicknamed "Elvis the Pelvis" (television cameras were not permitted to film below his waist).  
  
In 1956, following his six television appearances on The Dorsey Brothers' "Stage Show", Elvis was cast in his first acting role, in a supporting part in [Love Me Tender (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049452/?ls), the first of 33 movies he starred in.  
  
In 1958, Elvis was drafted into the military, and relocated to Bad Nauheim, Germany. There he met 14-year old army damsel Priscilla Ann Wagner ([Priscilla Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001636/?ls)), whom he would eventually marry after an eight-year courtship, and by whom he had his only child, [Lisa Marie Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1070086/?ls). Elvis' military service and the "British Invasion" of the 1960s reduced his concerts, though not his movie/recording income.  
  
Through the 1960s, Elvis settled in Hollywood, where he starred in the majority of his thirty-three movies, mainly musicals, acting alongside some of the most well known actors in Hollywood. Critics panned most of his films, but they did very well at the box office, earning upwards of $150 million total. His last fiction film, [Change of Habit (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065537/?ls), deals with several social issues; romance within the clergy, an autistic child, almost unheard of in 1969, rape, and mob violence. It has recently received critical acclaim.  
  
Elvis made a comeback in the 1970s with live concert appearances starting in early 1970 in Las Vegas with over 57 sold-out shows. He toured throughout the United States, appearing on-stage in over 500 live appearances, many of them sold out shows. His marriage ended in divorce, and the stress of constantly traveling as well as his increasing weight gain and dependence upon stimulants and depressants took their toll.  
  
Elvis Presley died at age 42 on August 16, 1977 at his mansion in Graceland, near Memphis, shocking his fans worldwide. At the time of his death, he had sold more than 600 million singles and albums. Since his death, Graceland has become a shrine for millions of followers worldwide. Elvis impersonators and purported sightings have become stock subjects for humorists. To date, Elvis Presley is the only performer to have been inducted into three separate music 'Halls of Fame'. Throughout his career, he set records for concert attendance, television ratings and recordings sales, and remains one of the best-selling and most influential artists in the history of popular music.

Kelly was actively involved in education, drug reform and many charitable organizations. She was acknowledged with numerous awards as a result of her work. She married [John Travolta](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000237/?ls) on September 12, 1991, and they had three children.  
  
Kelly died on July 12, 2020, in Ocala, Florida, after a two-year battle with breast cancer. She was 57.

Elegant blonde Nicole Kidman, known as one of Hollywood's top Australian imports, was actually born in Honolulu, Hawaii, to Anthony (a biochemist and clinical psychologist) and Janelle (a nursing instructor) Kidman. The family moved almost immediately to Washington, D.C., where Nicole's father pursued his research on breast cancer, then, three years later, they made the pilgrimage to her parents' native Sydney, Australia. Young Nicole's first love was ballet, but she eventually took up mime and drama as well. (Her first stage role was a bleating sheep in an elementary school Christmas pageant.) In her adolescent years, acting edged out the other arts and became a kind of refuge; as her classmates sought out fun in the sun, the fair-skinned Kidman retreated to dark rehearsal halls to practice her craft. She worked regularly at the Philip Street Theater, where she once received a personal letter of praise and encouragement from audience member [Jane Campion](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001005/?ls) (then a film student). Kidman eventually dropped out of high school to pursue acting full-time. She broke into movies at age 16, landing a role in the Australian holiday favorite [Bush Christmas (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085282/?ls). That appearance touched off a flurry of film and television offers, including a lead in [BMX Bandits (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085204/?ls) and a turn as a schoolgirl-turned-protester in the miniseries [Vietnam (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0140770/?ls), for which she won her first Australian Film Institute Award. With the help of an American agent, she eventually made her U.S. debut, opposite [Sam Neill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000554/?ls), in the at-sea thriller [Dead Calm (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097162/?ls).  
  
Kidman's next casting coup scored her more than exposure. While starring as [Tom Cruise](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000129/?ls)'s doctor/love interest in the racetrack romance [Days of Thunder (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099371/?ls), she won over the Hollywood hunk hook, line and sinker. After a whirlwind courtship (and decent box office returns), the couple wed on December 24, 1990. Determined not to let her new marital status overshadow her fledgling career, the actress pressed on. She appeared as a catty high school senior in the Australian film [Flirting (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101898/?ls), then as [Dustin Hoffman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000163/?ls)'s moll in the gangster flick [Billy Bathgate (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101453/?ls). She reunited with Cruise for [Far and Away (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104231/?ls), the story of young Irish lovers who flee to America in the late 1800s, and starred opposite [Michael Keaton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000474/?ls) in the tear-tugger [My Life (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107630/?ls). Despite her steady employment, critics and moviegoers still had not quite warmed to Kidman as a leading lady. She tried to spice up her image by seducing [Val Kilmer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000174/?ls) in [Batman Forever (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112462/?ls), but achieved her real breakthrough with [Gus Van Sant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001814/?ls)'s [To Die For (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114681/?ls). As a fame-crazed housewife determined to eliminate any obstacle in her path, Kidman proved that she had impressive range and deadly comic timing. She took home a Golden Globe and several critics' awards for the performance. In 1996, Kidman stepped into a corset to work with her countrywoman and onetime admirer, [Jane Campion](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001005/?ls), on the adaptation of [Henry James](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0416556/?ls)'s [The Portrait of a Lady (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117364/?ls). A few months later, she tore across the screen as a nuclear weapons expert in [The Peacemaker (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119874/?ls), adding "action star" to her professional repertoire.  
  
She and Cruise then disappeared into a notoriously long, secretive shoot for [Stanley Kubrick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000040/?ls)'s sexual thriller [Eyes Wide Shut (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120663/?ls). The couple's on-screen shenanigans prompted an increase in public speculation about their sex life. (Rumors had long been circulating that their marriage was a cover-up for Cruise's rumored homosexuality.) Tired of denying tabloid attacks, they successfully sued 'The Star' for a story alleging that they needed a sex therapist to coach them through love scenes.  
  
Family life has always been a priority for Kidman. Born to social activists (her mother was a feminist; her father, a labor advocate), Nicole and her younger sister, [Antonia Kidman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1159418/?ls), had discussed current events around the dinner table and participated in their parents' campaigns by passing out pamphlets on street corners. When Nicole was 17, her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer; Nicole stopped working and took a massage course so that she could provide physical therapy. (Her mother eventually beat the cancer.) Kidman and Cruise adopted two children: Isabella Jane (born 1992) and Connor Antony (born 1995). Despite their rock-solid image, the couple announced in early 2001 that they were separating due to career conflicts. Her marriage to Cruise ended mid-summer of 2001.

Jennifer Garner, who catapulted into stardom with her lead role on the television series [Alias (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285333/?ls), has come a long way from her birthplace of Houston, Texas. Raised in Charleston, West Virginia by her mother Patricia Ann (née English), a retired English teacher, and her father, Billy Jack Garner, a former chemical engineer, she is the second of their three daughters. She spent nine years of her adolescence studying ballet, and characterizes her years in dance as consisting of determination rather than talent, being driven mostly by a love of the stage.  
  
Jennifer took this determination with her when she enrolled at Denison University as a chemistry major; later she changed her major when she discovered that her passion for the stage was stronger than her love of science. New York attracted the young actress after college, and she worked as a hostess while pursuing a career in film and television. Her most recent move has been to Los Angeles, a decision that led to a role on the television series [Felicity (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0134247/?ls), where she met her future husband [Scott Foley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004930/?ls). The couple divorced in 2004.  
  
Jennifer starred in the television series [Alias (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285333/?ls) as Agent Sydney Bristow, who works for the Central Intelligence Agency. For her work, Garner has received four consecutive Emmy nominations for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series. She has also received four Golden Globe nominations and won once, as well as received two Screen Actors Guild Award nominations, and won once. She has appeared in numerous other television production as well as such films as [Elektra (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0357277/?ls), [13 Going on 30 (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0337563/?ls), [Daredevil (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0287978/?ls), [Pearl Harbor (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0213149/?ls) and [Dude, Where's My Car? (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0242423/?ls). Aside from filming [Alias (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285333/?ls), Jennifer enjoys cooking, gardening, hiking, and--inspired by her character on the series--kickboxing. She married actor and filmmaker [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ls) in 2005, now her ex-husband, with whom she has three children.

 #### [33. Cara Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930209/?ref_=ls_t_33) 

    *   Actress
    *   Soundtrack

[The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ref_=ls_knf_33)

Perky, talented, blue-eyed redhead Cara Williams had acting aspirations from the get-go. She was born in Brooklyn on June 29, 1925, as Bernice Kamiat, to an Austrian Jewish father, Benjamin Kamiat, and a mother of Romanian Jewish descent, Flora (Schwartz). Cara began performing as a child and continued into her teens. After her parents' divorce, she relocated with her mother to Hollywood where she attended the Hollywood Professional School and lent her voice to both radio and animated cartoon shorts. At age 16 she was signed by 20th Century-Fox and began to play minor, often unbilled parts in drama, comedy and musicals billing herself as Bernice Kay.  
  
Throughout WWII she was always reliable for adding a little pep and zing to her smallish roles. She played various shapely secretaries, salesgirls, girlfriends, etc. in such minor fodder as [Wide Open Town (1941)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0034391/?ls), [Happy Land (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035970/?ls), [In the Meantime, Darling (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036955/?ls) and [Don Juan Quilligan (1945)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0037655/?ls), but nothing to propel her into the front ranks.  
  
Things started picking up in the post-war years. She made a splash on stage in a production of "Born Yesterday" and started earning notably feisty, tart-tongued roles in such films as [Boomerang! (1947)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0039208/?ls) and [The Saxon Charm (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040759/?ls). By the 1950s she showed scene-stealing potential in [The Girl Next Door (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045815/?ls) and [The Helen Morgan Story (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050494/?ls), and finally earned an Academy Award nomination for her sad, touching supporting turn as a widowed mother in the classic [The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ls) opposite [Sidney Poitier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001627/?ls) and [Tony Curtis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000348/?ls). This led to a couple of flashy gangster moll roles in the film comedies [Never Steal Anything Small (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053109/?ls) and [The Man from the Diners' Club (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057284/?ls).  
  
The sitcom [December Bride (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046592/?ls) starring [Spring Byington](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001981/?ls) had deadpan quipster [Harry Morgan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0604702/?ls) stealing many scenes griping about scatterbrained wife Gladys (who was never shown on camera). When Morgan moved into his own spinoff series, Gladys was finally revealed in the form of Cara on the initially popular [Pete and Gladys (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053529/?ls) TV show. The program did not last as long as it deserved (two seasons) but the dusky-voiced Cara came off well and was escorted directly into her own series [The Cara Williams Show (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057739/?ls) with the equally personable [Frank Aletter](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0018173/?ls) at her side. Molded at this time by the CBS powers-that-be as the next wacky redhead to follow in the comedy heels of [Lucille Ball](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000840/?ls), the plans quickly went askew following an unfavorable network power shuffle and the canceling of her sitcom after only one season. With her momentum completely gone, her career went into rapid decline. She did manage a steady role on the first season of [Rhoda (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071040/?ls), and an affecting dramatic turn in the ensemble film soaper [Doctors' Wives (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067004/?ls). By the 1980s, however, she had officially retired.  
  
A turbulent 1950s marriage to actor [John Drew Barrymore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000857/?ls) (who later became the father of actress Drew in a subsequent marriage) produced son [John Blyth Barrymore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0058213/?ls) who went into acting as well and appeared in a bit role in his mother's last film [Dead on Arrival (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078032/?ls). Cara subsequently married a Beverly Hills realtor (her third husband) and later displayed a strong business acumen in interior designing and as a champion poker player. She also had one child from her first marriage.

Her mother was of Irish descent and her father had French, English, German, and Scottish ancestry.  
  
Jackie lived in posh penthouse apartments in New York City until her parents divorced when she was about six. Several years later her mother married Hugh D. Auchincloss and Jackie became the stepsister of two brothers and a sister from Hugh's previous marriages. Soon there were another brother and sister as a result of the new marriage.  
  
Jackie attended boarding schools and then Vassar. After two years, though, she got tired of schools and spent her junior year studying at the Sorbonne in Paris. When she got back to the US she did not want to go back to Vassar, so she enrolled in George Washington University in Washington, DC, graduating in 1951. She took a job at the CIA and in January of 1952 went to work at a Washington newspaper as a photographer. During an assignment, she met U.S. Senator [John F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448123/?ls), who was 12 years her senior. They were married on September 12, 1953. After having one stillborn daughter, Arabella Kennedy, along came [Caroline Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447952/?ls), on November 27, 1957. Their first son [John Kennedy Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447882/?ls), who was born on November 25, 1960. In 1961 John Kennedy became the 35th President of the US. Jackie spent the White House years doing her best to save the historical landmarks around Washington. In August of 1963 she went into labor with their fourth child, Patrick Bouvier Kennedy, but sadly, he died shortly after birth. Jackie was not scheduled to go to Texas with her husband, but decided to go as a means of perhaps putting the death of Patrick behind them. She was sitting next to him in the open-air limousine on November 22, 1963, when JFK was assassinated.  
  
In 1968 her brother-in-law, [Robert F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448305/?ls), was also assassinated. The combination of the death of two children and the murders of her husband and brother-in-law proved to be too much for her, and she came to the conclusion that she and her family could not live safely in the US any longer. On October 20, 1968, she married Greek shipping magnate, [Aristotle Onassis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1238516/?ls). After he died in the mid-'70s she returned to New York and became a book editor. She dedicated the last 20 years of her life to her children, her grandchildren and her friend [Maurice Tempelsman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4935215/?ls). In the early 1990s she found out she had non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and died on May 19, 1994. Shortly after her death there was a sale of some of her prized possessions. [Arnold Schwarzenegger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000216/?ls) spent more than a million dollars on some of the things to honor the aunt and uncle of his wife, [Maria Shriver](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005425/?ls). John Fitzgerald Kennedy Jr. was born on November 25, 1960, in Washington, DC, to John Fitzgerald Kennedy (President-to-be [John F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448123/?ls)) and Jacqueline Lee Bouvier Kennedy ([Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448080/?ls)). Three weeks before his birth, his father was elected President of the United States, and the nation loved little John. The press dubbed him "John-John", but his family called him John. Even as a toddler, he loved to fly. On his third birthday, his father was buried, and he was photographed giving his father's casket a salute in a photo and video seen around the world. About a month later, they moved out of the White House and into a 15-room apartment overlooking Central Park in New York City. He went to private schools. When he was six, his uncle [Robert F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448305/?ls) was assassinated while running for president. He had been a father figure to John and his sister, [Caroline Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447952/?ls), a fact that [Ethel Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448026/?ls) -- who had nine children with RFK -- did not like. That same year, Jackie married Greek shipping magnate Aristotle Socrates (Ari) Onasis ([Aristotle Onassis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1238516/?ls)). He virtually played no part in John's life because John hardly saw him. Ari died in 1975. John went on to high school and then decided to go to Brown University in Rhode Island. He graduated and, after his mother said no to his becoming an actor, went to law school and became an assistant District Attorney. In 1994, Jackie died of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. In 1996, John married [Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4637138/?ls) on an island off Georgia. She was very shy, and that did not bode well because they were constantly being photographed. On July 16th, 1999, Carolyn and her sister Lauren, with John as pilot, took off in his plane for Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts, to drop Lauren off, with John and Carolyn continuing onward to the Kennedy Compound for the wedding of his cousin [Rory Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448311/?ls) (Robert's youngest daughter, born after RFK's death). It was foggy, and several miles off Martha's Vineyard, the plane crashed, killing all three of them. The bodies of the women were found near the wreckage, but John's body was found in the pilot's seat.

Their daughters would have a stable, middle-class upbringing.  
  
Jennifer always dreamed of being a multi-tasking superstar. As a child, she enjoyed a variety of musical genres, mainly Afro-Caribbean rhythms like salsa, merengue, and bachata, and mainstream music like pop, hip-hop, and R&B. Although she loved music, the film industry also intrigued her. Her biggest influence was the [Rita Moreno](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001549/?ls) musical, [West Side Story (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055614/?ls). At 5, Jennifer began taking singing and dancing lessons. Aside from being a budding entertainer, Jennifer was also a Catholic schoolgirl, attending eight years at a Catholic elementary school named Holy Family, located in The Bronx, before graduating from all-girls prep school Preston High School after a four-year stay. At school, Jennifer was an amazing athlete and participated in track and field and tennis. She spent most of her upbringing in a two-story house in the Castle Hill neighborhood.  
  
At 18, Jennifer moved out of her parents' home. After high school, she briefly worked in a law office and took dance classes at night. During this time, she continued dance classes at night. Her big break came when she was offered a job as a fly girl on Fox's hit comedy [In Living Color (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098830/?ls). After a two-year stay at [In Living Color (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098830/?ls) where actress [Rosie Perez](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001609/?ls) served as choreographer, Lopez then went on to dance for famed singer-actress [Janet Jackson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001390/?ls). Her first major film was [Gregory Nava](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0622695/?ls)'s [My Family (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0113896/?ls), and her career went into overdrive when she portrayed late Tejana singer [Selena](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0702373/?ls) in [Selena (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120094/?ls).

Born on February 1, 1965 to [Bruce Lee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000045/?ls) (Martial Arts idol) and [Linda Lee Cadwell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004791/?ls). Brother to [Shannon Lee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005135/?ls). In 1970-71, they moved to Hong Kong, where Brandon lived until age eight, becoming fluent in Cantonese. By the time he was able to walk, he was already involved in learning about martial arts from his father.  
  
Brandon attended high school in Los Angeles, where he realized that he had also inherited acting ability along with his martial arts skills. In 1983, he was expelled from school because of misbehavior, but received his diploma at Miraleste High School. He continued his education and interest in acting at Emerson College in Massachusetts, where he majored in theatre. Having chosen an acting career, he studied at the Strasberg Academy, with [Eric Morris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0606519/?ls) in New York and in Los Angeles, and in [Lynette Katselas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1227919/?ls)' class in Los Angeles.  
  
His first professional job as an actor came at age twenty, when casting director [Lynn Stalmaster](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002679/?ls) asked him to read for a CBS television film, [Kung Fu: The Movie (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091361/?ls). Lee's first role in a feature film was [Legacy of Rage (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091428/?ls) (aka "Legacy of Rage" (1986)) for D.M. Films of Hong Kong, followed by a co-starring role in [Showdown in Little Tokyo (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102915/?ls). He was also in [Rapid Fire (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105219/?ls), and [The Crow (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109506/?ls). He turned down offers to be in [Dragon: The Bruce Lee Story (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106770/?ls).  
  
Brandon died (while filming) at the age of 28, of what is to be believed, a brain hemorrhage on the set of [The Crow (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109506/?ls). The film crew shot a scene in which it was decided to use a gun without consent from the weapons coordinator, who had been sent home early that night. They handed [Michael Massee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0557219/?ls) the gun loaded with full power blanks and shot the scene, unaware that a bullet had become dislodged from a previous shot and had lodged itself in the barrel. Upon shooting of the scene the blank round forced the bullet out the barrel striking Brandon Lee. The crew only noticed when Lee was slow getting up. The doctors worked desperately for five hours, but it was no use. The bullet had lodged itself in Mr Lee's lower spine. He was pronounced dead at 1:04 P.M. the next day. He was supposed to marry [Eliza Hutton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1545105/?ls) on April 17, 1993. His body was flown to Seattle to be buried beside his father in Lake View Cemetery.

 #### [3. Lucille Ball](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000840/?ref_=ls_t_3) 

    *   Producer
    *   Actress
    *   Production Manager

[I Love Lucy (1951–1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043208/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

The woman who will always be remembered as the crazy, accident-prone, lovable Lucy Ricardo was born Lucille Desiree Ball on August 6, 1911 in Jamestown, New York, the daughter of Desiree Evelyn "DeDe" (Hunt) and Henry Durrell "Had" Ball. Her father died before she was four, and her mother worked several jobs, so she and her younger brother were raised by their grandparents. Always willing to take responsibility for her brother and young cousins, she was a restless teenager who yearned to "make some noise". She entered a dramatic school in New York City, but while her classmate [Bette Davis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000012/?ls) received all the raves, she was sent home; "too shy". She found some work modeling for [Hattie Carnegie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0138651/?ls)'s and, in 1933, she was chosen to be a "Goldwyn Girl" and appear in the film [Roman Scandals (1933)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0024507/?ls).  
  
She was put under contract to RKO Radio Pictures and several small roles, including one in [Top Hat (1935)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0027125/?ls), followed. Eventually, she received starring roles in B-pictures and, occasionally, a good role in an A-picture, like in [Stage Door (1937)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0029604/?ls) or [The Big Street (1942)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0034514/?ls). While filming [Too Many Girls (1940)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0033173/?ls), she met and fell madly in love with a young Cuban actor-musician named [Desi Arnaz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000789/?ls). Despite different personalities, lifestyles, religions and ages (he was six years younger), he fell hard, too, and after a passionate romance, they eloped and were married in November 1940. Lucy soon switched to Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, where she got better roles in films such as [Du Barry Was a Lady (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035829/?ls); [Best Foot Forward (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035675/?ls) and the [Katharine Hepburn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000031/?ls)-[Spencer Tracy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000075/?ls) vehicle [Without Love (1945)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038256/?ls). In 1948, she took a starring role in the radio comedy "My Favorite Husband", in which she played the scatterbrained wife of a Midwestern banker. In 1950, CBS came knocking with the offer of turning it into a television series. After convincing the network brass to let Desi play her husband and to sign over the rights to and creative control over the series to them, work began on the most popular and universally beloved sitcom of all time.  
  
With [I Love Lucy (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043208/?ls), she and Desi promoted the 3-camera technique now the standard in filming sitcoms using 35mm film (the earliest known example of the 3-camera technique is the first Russian feature film, "Defence of Sevastopol" in 1911). Desi syndicated I Love Lucy. Lucille Ball was the first woman to own her own studio as the head of Desilu Productions.  
  
Lucille Ball died at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, age 77, of an acute aortic aneurysm on April 26, 1989 in Los Angeles, CA.

[Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

Clinton Eastwood Jr. was born May 31, 1930 in San Francisco, to Clinton Eastwood Sr., a bond salesman and later manufacturing executive for Georgia-Pacific Corporation, and [Ruth Wood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2503495/?ls) (née Margret Ruth Runner), a housewife turned IBM clerk. He grew up in nearby Piedmont. At school Clint took interest in music and mechanics, but was an otherwise bored student; this resulted in being held back a grade.  
  
In 1949, the year he graduated from high school, his parents and younger sister Jeanne moved to Seattle. Clint spent a couple years in the Pacific Northwest himself, operating log broncs in Springfield, Oregon, with summer gigs life-guarding in Renton, Washington. Returning to California in 1951, he did a two-year stint at Fort Ord Military Reservation and later enrolled at L.A. City College, but dropped out to pursue acting.  
  
During the mid-1950s he landed uncredited bit parts in such Z movies as [Revenge of the Creature (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048554/?ls) and [Tarantula (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048696/?ls) while digging swimming pools and driving a garbage truck to supplement his income. In 1958, he landed his first consequential acting role in the long-running TV show [Rawhide (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052504/?ls) with [Eric Fleming](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281661/?ls). Although only a secondary player the first seven seasons, he was promoted to series star when Fleming departed--both literally and figuratively--in its final year, along the way becoming a recognizable face to television viewers around the country.  
  
Eastwood's big-screen breakthrough came as The Man with No Name in [Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ls)'s trilogy of excellent spaghetti westerns: [A Fistful of Dollars (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058461/?ls), [For a Few Dollars More (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059578/?ls), and [The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060196/?ls). The movies were shown exclusively in Italy during their respective copyright years with [Enrico Maria Salerno](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0758066/?ls) providing the voice of Eastwood's character, finally getting American distribution in 1967-68. As the last film racked up respectable grosses, Eastwood, 37, rose from a barely registering actor to sought-after commodity in just a matter of months. Again a success was the late-blooming star's first U.S.-made western, [Hang 'Em High (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061747/?ls). He followed that up with the lead role in [Coogan's Bluff (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062824/?ls) (the loose inspiration for the TV series [McCloud (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065317/?ls)), before playing second fiddle to [Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ls) in the World War II epic [Where Eagles Dare (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065207/?ls) and [Lee Marvin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001511/?ls) in the bizarre musical [Paint Your Wagon (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064782/?ls). In [Two Mules for Sister Sara (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065134/?ls) and [Kelly's Heroes (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065938/?ls), Eastwood leaned in an experimental direction by combining tough-guy action with offbeat humor.  
  
1971 proved to be his busiest year in film. He starred as a sleazy Union soldier in [The Beguiled (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066819/?ls) to critical acclaim, and made his directorial debut with the classic erotic thriller [Play Misty for Me (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067588/?ls). His role as the hard edge police inspector in [Dirty Harry (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066999/?ls), meanwhile, boosted him to cultural icon status and helped popularize the loose-cannon cop genre. Eastwood put out a steady stream of entertaining movies thereafter: the westerns [Joe Kidd (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068768/?ls), [High Plains Drifter (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068699/?ls) and [The Outlaw Josey Wales (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075029/?ls) (his first of six onscreen collaborations with then live-in love [Sondra Locke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0516800/?ls)), the Dirty Harry sequels [Magnum Force (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070355/?ls) and [The Enforcer (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074483/?ls), the action-packed road adventures [Thunderbolt and Lightfoot (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072288/?ls) and [The Gauntlet (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076070/?ls), and the prison film [Escape from Alcatraz (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079116/?ls). He branched out into the comedy genre in 1978 with [Every Which Way But Loose (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077523/?ls), which became the biggest hit of his career up to that time; taking inflation into account, it still is. In short, [The Eiger Sanction (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072926/?ls) notwithstanding, the 1970s were nonstop success for Eastwood.  
  
Eastwood kicked off the 1980s with [Any Which Way You Can (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080377/?ls), the blockbuster sequel to Every Which Way but Loose. The fourth Dirty Harry film, [Sudden Impact (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086383/?ls), was the highest-grossing film of the franchise and spawned his trademark catchphrase: "Make my day." He also starred in [Bronco Billy (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080472/?ls), [Firefox (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083943/?ls), [Tightrope (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088272/?ls), [City Heat (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087062/?ls), [Pale Rider (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089767/?ls) and [Heartbreak Ridge (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091187/?ls), all of which were solid hits, with [Honkytonk Man (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084088/?ls) being his only commercial failure of the period. In 1988, he did his fifth and final Dirty Harry movie, [The Dead Pool (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094963/?ls). Although it was a success overall, it did not have the box office punch the previous films had. About this time, with outright bombs like [Pink Cadillac (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098097/?ls) and [The Rookie (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100514/?ls), it seemed Eastwood's star was declining as it never had before. He then started taking on low-key projects, directing [Bird (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094747/?ls), a biopic of [Charlie Parker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0662127/?ls) that earned him a Golden Globe, and starring in and directing [White Hunter Black Heart (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100928/?ls), an uneven, loose biopic of [John Huston](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001379/?ls) (both films had a limited release).  
  
Eastwood bounced back big time with his dark western [Unforgiven (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105695/?ls), which garnered the then 62-year-old his first ever Academy Award nomination (Best Actor), and an Oscar win for Best Director. Churning out a quick follow-up hit, he took on the secret service in [In the Line of Fire (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107206/?ls), then accepted second billing for the first time since 1970 in the interesting but poorly received [A Perfect World (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107808/?ls) with [Kevin Costner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000126/?ls). Next was a love story, [The Bridges of Madison County (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112579/?ls), where Eastwood surprised audiences with a sensitive performance alongside none other than [Meryl Streep](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000658/?ls). But it soon became apparent he was going backwards after his brief revival. Subsequent films were credible, but nothing really stuck out. [Absolute Power (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118548/?ls) and [Space Cowboys (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0186566/?ls) did well enough, while [True Crime (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0139668/?ls) and [Blood Work (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0309377/?ls) were received badly, as was [Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119668/?ls), which he directed but didn't appear in.  
  
Eastwood surprised again in the mid-2000s, returning to the top of the A-list with [Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ls). Also starring [Hilary Swank](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005476/?ls) and [Morgan Freeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000151/?ls), the hugely successful drama won four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director for Eastwood. He scored his second Best Actor nomination, too. His next starring vehicle, [Gran Torino (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1205489/?ls), earned almost $30 million in its opening weekend and was his highest grosser unadjusted for inflation. 2012 saw him in a rare lighthearted movie, [Trouble with the Curve (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2083383/?ls), as well as a reality show, [Mrs. Eastwood & Company (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2305717/?ls).  
  
Between acting jobs, he chalked up an impressive list of credits behind the camera. He directed [Mystic River (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0327056/?ls) (in which [Sean Penn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000576/?ls) and [Tim Robbins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000209/?ls) gave Oscar-winning performances), [Flags of Our Fathers (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0418689/?ls), [Letters from Iwo Jima (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0498380/?ls) (nominated for the Best Picture Oscar), [Changeling (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0824747/?ls) (a vehicle for [Angelina Jolie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001401/?ls)), [Invictus (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1057500/?ls) (again with Freeman), [Hereafter (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1212419/?ls), [J. Edgar (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1616195/?ls), [Jersey Boys (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1742044/?ls), [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ls) (2014's top box office champ), [Sully (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3263904/?ls) (starring [Tom Hanks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000158/?ls) as hero pilot [Chesley Sullenberger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3314810/?ls)) and [The 15:17 to Paris (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6802308/?ls). Back on screens after a considerable absence, he played an unlikely drug courier in [The Mule (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7959026/?ls), which reached the top of the box office with a nine-figure gross, then directed [Richard Jewell (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3513548/?ls). At age 91, Eastwood made history as the oldest actor to star above the title in a movie with the release of [Cry Macho (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1924245/?ls).  
  
Away from the limelight, Eastwood has led an aberrant existence and is described by biographer [Patrick McGilligan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0569292/?ls) as a cunning manipulator of the media. His convoluted slew of partners and children are now somewhat factually acknowledged, but for the first three decades of his celebrity, his personal life was kept top secret, and several of his families were left out of the official narrative. The actor refuses to disclose his exact number of offspring even to this day. He had a longtime relationship with similarly abstruse co-star Locke (who died aged 74 in 2018, though for her entire public life she masqueraded about being younger), and has fathered at least eight children by at least six different women in an unending string of liaisons, many of which overlapped. He has been married only twice, however, with a mere three of his progeny coming from those unions.  
  
His known children are: [Laurie Murray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm15158933/?ls) (b. 1954), whose mother is unidentified; [Kimber Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247761/?ls) (b. 1964) with stuntwoman [Roxanne Tunis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0876651/?ls); [Kyle Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247762/?ls) (b. 1968) and [Alison Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002055/?ls) (b. 1972) with his first ex-wife, [Margaret Neville Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1527881/?ls); [Scott Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2207222/?ls) (b. 1986) and [Kathryn Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1828228/?ls) (b. 1988) with stewardess Jacelyn Reeves; [Francesca Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247754/?ls) (b. 1993) with actress [Frances Fisher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004920/?ls); and [Morgan Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1765859/?ls) (b. 1996) with his second ex-wife, [Dina Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247753/?ls). The entire time that he lived with Locke she was legally married to sculptor [Gordon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026770/?ls).  
  
Eastwood has real estate holdings in Bel-Air, La Quinta, Carmel-by-the-Sea, Cassel (in remote northern California), Idaho's Sun Valley and Kihei, Hawaii.

Elvis Aaron Presley was born on January 8, 1935 in East Tupelo, Mississippi, to [Gladys Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0696175/?ls) (née Gladys Love Smith) and [Vernon Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0696184/?ls) (Vernon Elvis Presley). He had a twin brother who was stillborn. In 1948, Elvis and his parents moved to Memphis, Tennessee where he attended Humes High School. In 1953, he attended the senior prom with the current girl he was courting, Regis Wilson. After graduating from high school in Memphis, Elvis took odd jobs working as a movie theater usher and a truck driver for Crown Electric Company. He began singing locally as "The Hillbilly Cat", then signed with a local recording company, and then with RCA in 1955.  
  
Elvis did much to establish early rock and roll music. He began his career as a performer of rockabilly, an up-tempo fusion of country music and rhythm and blues, with a strong backbeat. His novel versions of existing songs, mixing 'black' and 'white' sounds, made him popular - and controversial - as did his uninhibited stage and television performances. He recorded songs in the rock and roll genre, with tracks like "Jailhouse Rock" and "Hound Dog" later embodying the style. Presley had a versatile voice and had unusually wide success encompassing other genres, including gospel, blues, ballads and pop music. Teenage girls became hysterical over his blatantly sexual gyrations, particularly the one that got him nicknamed "Elvis the Pelvis" (television cameras were not permitted to film below his waist).  
  
In 1956, following his six television appearances on The Dorsey Brothers' "Stage Show", Elvis was cast in his first acting role, in a supporting part in [Love Me Tender (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049452/?ls), the first of 33 movies he starred in.  
  
In 1958, Elvis was drafted into the military, and relocated to Bad Nauheim, Germany. There he met 14-year old army damsel Priscilla Ann Wagner ([Priscilla Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001636/?ls)), whom he would eventually marry after an eight-year courtship, and by whom he had his only child, [Lisa Marie Presley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1070086/?ls). Elvis' military service and the "British Invasion" of the 1960s reduced his concerts, though not his movie/recording income.  
  
Through the 1960s, Elvis settled in Hollywood, where he starred in the majority of his thirty-three movies, mainly musicals, acting alongside some of the most well known actors in Hollywood. Critics panned most of his films, but they did very well at the box office, earning upwards of $150 million total. His last fiction film, [Change of Habit (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065537/?ls), deals with several social issues; romance within the clergy, an autistic child, almost unheard of in 1969, rape, and mob violence. It has recently received critical acclaim.  
  
Elvis made a comeback in the 1970s with live concert appearances starting in early 1970 in Las Vegas with over 57 sold-out shows. He toured throughout the United States, appearing on-stage in over 500 live appearances, many of them sold out shows. His marriage ended in divorce, and the stress of constantly traveling as well as his increasing weight gain and dependence upon stimulants and depressants took their toll.  
  
Elvis Presley died at age 42 on August 16, 1977 at his mansion in Graceland, near Memphis, shocking his fans worldwide. At the time of his death, he had sold more than 600 million singles and albums. Since his death, Graceland has become a shrine for millions of followers worldwide. Elvis impersonators and purported sightings have become stock subjects for humorists. To date, Elvis Presley is the only performer to have been inducted into three separate music 'Halls of Fame'. Throughout his career, he set records for concert attendance, television ratings and recordings sales, and remains one of the best-selling and most influential artists in the history of popular music.

Elegant blonde Nicole Kidman, known as one of Hollywood's top Australian imports, was actually born in Honolulu, Hawaii, to Anthony (a biochemist and clinical psychologist) and Janelle (a nursing instructor) Kidman. The family moved almost immediately to Washington, D.C., where Nicole's father pursued his research on breast cancer, then, three years later, they made the pilgrimage to her parents' native Sydney, Australia. Young Nicole's first love was ballet, but she eventually took up mime and drama as well. (Her first stage role was a bleating sheep in an elementary school Christmas pageant.) In her adolescent years, acting edged out the other arts and became a kind of refuge; as her classmates sought out fun in the sun, the fair-skinned Kidman retreated to dark rehearsal halls to practice her craft. She worked regularly at the Philip Street Theater, where she once received a personal letter of praise and encouragement from audience member [Jane Campion](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001005/?ls) (then a film student). Kidman eventually dropped out of high school to pursue acting full-time. She broke into movies at age 16, landing a role in the Australian holiday favorite [Bush Christmas (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085282/?ls). That appearance touched off a flurry of film and television offers, including a lead in [BMX Bandits (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085204/?ls) and a turn as a schoolgirl-turned-protester in the miniseries [Vietnam (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0140770/?ls), for which she won her first Australian Film Institute Award. With the help of an American agent, she eventually made her U.S. debut, opposite [Sam Neill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000554/?ls), in the at-sea thriller [Dead Calm (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097162/?ls).  
  
Kidman's next casting coup scored her more than exposure. While starring as [Tom Cruise](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000129/?ls)'s doctor/love interest in the racetrack romance [Days of Thunder (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099371/?ls), she won over the Hollywood hunk hook, line and sinker. After a whirlwind courtship (and decent box office returns), the couple wed on December 24, 1990. Determined not to let her new marital status overshadow her fledgling career, the actress pressed on. She appeared as a catty high school senior in the Australian film [Flirting (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101898/?ls), then as [Dustin Hoffman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000163/?ls)'s moll in the gangster flick [Billy Bathgate (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101453/?ls). She reunited with Cruise for [Far and Away (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104231/?ls), the story of young Irish lovers who flee to America in the late 1800s, and starred opposite [Michael Keaton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000474/?ls) in the tear-tugger [My Life (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107630/?ls). Despite her steady employment, critics and moviegoers still had not quite warmed to Kidman as a leading lady. She tried to spice up her image by seducing [Val Kilmer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000174/?ls) in [Batman Forever (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112462/?ls), but achieved her real breakthrough with [Gus Van Sant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001814/?ls)'s [To Die For (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114681/?ls). As a fame-crazed housewife determined to eliminate any obstacle in her path, Kidman proved that she had impressive range and deadly comic timing. She took home a Golden Globe and several critics' awards for the performance. In 1996, Kidman stepped into a corset to work with her countrywoman and onetime admirer, [Jane Campion](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001005/?ls), on the adaptation of [Henry James](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0416556/?ls)'s [The Portrait of a Lady (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117364/?ls). A few months later, she tore across the screen as a nuclear weapons expert in [The Peacemaker (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119874/?ls), adding "action star" to her professional repertoire.  
  
She and Cruise then disappeared into a notoriously long, secretive shoot for [Stanley Kubrick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000040/?ls)'s sexual thriller [Eyes Wide Shut (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120663/?ls). The couple's on-screen shenanigans prompted an increase in public speculation about their sex life. (Rumors had long been circulating that their marriage was a cover-up for Cruise's rumored homosexuality.) Tired of denying tabloid attacks, they successfully sued 'The Star' for a story alleging that they needed a sex therapist to coach them through love scenes.  
  
Family life has always been a priority for Kidman. Born to social activists (her mother was a feminist; her father, a labor advocate), Nicole and her younger sister, [Antonia Kidman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1159418/?ls), had discussed current events around the dinner table and participated in their parents' campaigns by passing out pamphlets on street corners. When Nicole was 17, her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer; Nicole stopped working and took a massage course so that she could provide physical therapy. (Her mother eventually beat the cancer.) Kidman and Cruise adopted two children: Isabella Jane (born 1992) and Connor Antony (born 1995). Despite their rock-solid image, the couple announced in early 2001 that they were separating due to career conflicts. Her marriage to Cruise ended mid-summer of 2001.

 #### [33. Cara Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930209/?ref_=ls_t_33) 

    *   Actress
    *   Soundtrack

[The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ref_=ls_knf_33)

Perky, talented, blue-eyed redhead Cara Williams had acting aspirations from the get-go. She was born in Brooklyn on June 29, 1925, as Bernice Kamiat, to an Austrian Jewish father, Benjamin Kamiat, and a mother of Romanian Jewish descent, Flora (Schwartz). Cara began performing as a child and continued into her teens. After her parents' divorce, she relocated with her mother to Hollywood where she attended the Hollywood Professional School and lent her voice to both radio and animated cartoon shorts. At age 16 she was signed by 20th Century-Fox and began to play minor, often unbilled parts in drama, comedy and musicals billing herself as Bernice Kay.  
  
Throughout WWII she was always reliable for adding a little pep and zing to her smallish roles. She played various shapely secretaries, salesgirls, girlfriends, etc. in such minor fodder as [Wide Open Town (1941)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0034391/?ls), [Happy Land (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035970/?ls), [In the Meantime, Darling (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036955/?ls) and [Don Juan Quilligan (1945)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0037655/?ls), but nothing to propel her into the front ranks.  
  
Things started picking up in the post-war years. She made a splash on stage in a production of "Born Yesterday" and started earning notably feisty, tart-tongued roles in such films as [Boomerang! (1947)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0039208/?ls) and [The Saxon Charm (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040759/?ls). By the 1950s she showed scene-stealing potential in [The Girl Next Door (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045815/?ls) and [The Helen Morgan Story (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050494/?ls), and finally earned an Academy Award nomination for her sad, touching supporting turn as a widowed mother in the classic [The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ls) opposite [Sidney Poitier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001627/?ls) and [Tony Curtis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000348/?ls). This led to a couple of flashy gangster moll roles in the film comedies [Never Steal Anything Small (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053109/?ls) and [The Man from the Diners' Club (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057284/?ls).  
  
The sitcom [December Bride (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046592/?ls) starring [Spring Byington](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001981/?ls) had deadpan quipster [Harry Morgan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0604702/?ls) stealing many scenes griping about scatterbrained wife Gladys (who was never shown on camera). When Morgan moved into his own spinoff series, Gladys was finally revealed in the form of Cara on the initially popular [Pete and Gladys (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053529/?ls) TV show. The program did not last as long as it deserved (two seasons) but the dusky-voiced Cara came off well and was escorted directly into her own series [The Cara Williams Show (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057739/?ls) with the equally personable [Frank Aletter](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0018173/?ls) at her side. Molded at this time by the CBS powers-that-be as the next wacky redhead to follow in the comedy heels of [Lucille Ball](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000840/?ls), the plans quickly went askew following an unfavorable network power shuffle and the canceling of her sitcom after only one season. With her momentum completely gone, her career went into rapid decline. She did manage a steady role on the first season of [Rhoda (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071040/?ls), and an affecting dramatic turn in the ensemble film soaper [Doctors' Wives (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067004/?ls). By the 1980s, however, she had officially retired.  
  
A turbulent 1950s marriage to actor [John Drew Barrymore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000857/?ls) (who later became the father of actress Drew in a subsequent marriage) produced son [John Blyth Barrymore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0058213/?ls) who went into acting as well and appeared in a bit role in his mother's last film [Dead on Arrival (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078032/?ls). Cara subsequently married a Beverly Hills realtor (her third husband) and later displayed a strong business acumen in interior designing and as a champion poker player. She also had one child from her first marriage.

Her mother was of Irish descent and her father had French, English, German, and Scottish ancestry.  
  
Jackie lived in posh penthouse apartments in New York City until her parents divorced when she was about six. Several years later her mother married Hugh D. Auchincloss and Jackie became the stepsister of two brothers and a sister from Hugh's previous marriages. Soon there were another brother and sister as a result of the new marriage.  
  
Jackie attended boarding schools and then Vassar. After two years, though, she got tired of schools and spent her junior year studying at the Sorbonne in Paris. When she got back to the US she did not want to go back to Vassar, so she enrolled in George Washington University in Washington, DC, graduating in 1951. She took a job at the CIA and in January of 1952 went to work at a Washington newspaper as a photographer. During an assignment, she met U.S. Senator [John F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448123/?ls), who was 12 years her senior. They were married on September 12, 1953. After having one stillborn daughter, Arabella Kennedy, along came [Caroline Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447952/?ls), on November 27, 1957. Their first son [John Kennedy Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447882/?ls), who was born on November 25, 1960. In 1961 John Kennedy became the 35th President of the US. Jackie spent the White House years doing her best to save the historical landmarks around Washington. In August of 1963 she went into labor with their fourth child, Patrick Bouvier Kennedy, but sadly, he died shortly after birth. Jackie was not scheduled to go to Texas with her husband, but decided to go as a means of perhaps putting the death of Patrick behind them. She was sitting next to him in the open-air limousine on November 22, 1963, when JFK was assassinated.  
  
In 1968 her brother-in-law, [Robert F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448305/?ls), was also assassinated. The combination of the death of two children and the murders of her husband and brother-in-law proved to be too much for her, and she came to the conclusion that she and her family could not live safely in the US any longer. On October 20, 1968, she married Greek shipping magnate, [Aristotle Onassis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1238516/?ls). After he died in the mid-'70s she returned to New York and became a book editor. She dedicated the last 20 years of her life to her children, her grandchildren and her friend [Maurice Tempelsman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4935215/?ls). In the early 1990s she found out she had non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and died on May 19, 1994. Shortly after her death there was a sale of some of her prized possessions.
